name: Baron Brisket
_identity: THREE TONS OF OPINION, ARRIVING LATE. All-wheel drive and 30000 N of shove make it the hardest launcher in the fleet -- and then drag 1.9 and top_speed 47 strangle it by about 41 m/s, because it is a brick with a lift kit. The rack is slow (steer_speed 4.2) and short (28 deg), the springs are soft for the mass (0.36 of critical), so it takes a full beat to lean, sets, and only then turns; brakes 38000 against 3050 kg is a long, nose-diving stop. handbrake_grip_mult 0.40 means it will not even slide properly -- it plows. Measured M16: hardest launch in the fleet (3.30 s to 20 m/s) and the longest stop by 6 m (41.9 m from 30 m/s), turning a 10.6 m circle against the cruiser's 7.7. The rollover threat is still the joke.
_tuning_math: corner mass = 3050/4 = 762.5 kg; static load = 762.5*9.81 = 7480.1 N; spring_rate 47000 N/m -> static compression = 7480.1/47000 = 0.1591 m = 28.9% of suspension_rest 0.55 (soft end of the 20-30% target: the lift kit has to WALLOW, not hold); critical damping = 2*sqrt(47000*762.5) = 11973 N*s/m; damping 4300 = 0.359 * critical, so the body pitches, rolls, and takes two beats to stop doing it. THE JOKE, INTACT: hardpoint -0.50 + 0.55 m of travel + 0.46 m tires put the body centre ~1.35 m above ground, and com_height 0.03 leaves the CoM right there at 1.381 m. Static rollover threshold = half-track / CoM height = 1.025/1.381 = ~0.74 g, and tire_friction 1.22 still supplies up to ~1.22 g -- the tires can always out-pull the geometry. Wide track and lazy damping delay it; physics wins anyway. Lateral forces act 0.53 m below the CoM, so it leans HARD out of every corner and lifts the inside wheels if thrown. Straight line: AWD grip = 1.22*3050*9.81 = 36505 N against 30000 N of engine, so it is ENGINE-limited at ~9.8 m/s^2 -- it out-drags everything and then loses the same race at 40 m/s.
